column1: Out of Control|1994|0|0||7,9,8,8,8,8,9,8,8,7|Kevin Kelly|Links distributed computing, evolution, markets and self-organization. Diverse examples illuminate feedback and decentralized control, but analogies between biological and engineered systems need explicit limits. Dated forecasts reduce durability somewhat without removing the underlying mechanisms.

The Spartan Regime: Its Character, Origins, and Grand Strategy|2016|10|10|-480|8,8,7,7,7,9,7,9,7,8|Paul A. Rahe|Connects Spartan institutions, social constraints and strategic choices. The institutional interpretation provides more than military chronology, but the evidence for early Sparta is limited and contested. Single-polity history and military-political centrality incur both deductions; endpoint 480 BCE approximates the early-regime focus.

Softwar|2003|0|0|2002|7,8,8,7,7,8,9,8,8,7|Matthew Symonds|Access-based history explains Oracle's competition, software business and leadership choices. Commercial and organizational mechanisms supply substantial transfer; Ellison's participation and comments create a perspective that requires critical distance. Technology business leads rather than celebrity as such.

Elon Musk|2015|0|0|2015|8,9,8,8,8,8,10,8,9,8|Ashlee Vance|Reported biography connects engineering ambition, capital, manufacturing constraints and company organization. Contrasting companies offer useful cases; personal narrative and limited access constrain causal attribution. This is Vance's biography, not Walter Isaacson's 2023 book.

Uncanny Valley|2020|10|0||7,7,6,6,7,8,7,7,9,8|Anna Wiener|Workplace memoir examines incentives, labor and status within technology companies. Situated observations expose organizational culture, with limited access to strategic or technical decisions. American social and workplace experience dominates; no fixed historical-period deduction is imposed on the contemporary memoir.

The Rise and Fall of Athens: Nine Greek Lives|100|10|10|-322|6,6,5,5,7,9,4,9,8,8|Plutarch|Ancient political biographies explore character, institutions and civic conflict, but anecdotal moral interpretation is not reliable causal identification. Comparison provides some reusable questions, with weak direct fit. Composition around 100 CE is approximate; the Greek lives reach the late fourth century BCE. Modern translation dates do not reset age.

Between Past and Future|1961|0|10||7,8,7,7,7,9,5,9,7,9|Hannah Arendt|Essays distinguish authority, freedom, education and historical judgment under modern conditions. Conceptual distinctions transfer across institutions, but historical interpretation and abstraction often exceed direct empirical support. Multiple essays offer independent payload without a single integrated system.

Republics Ancient and Modern|1992|10|10|1800|8,9,8,8,7,9,7,9,7,8|Paul A. Rahe|The source's singular title identifies Republics Ancient and Modern, a comparison of classical republicanism and its modern transformation. Extensive textual evidence supports distinctions, with substantial length and interpretive burden. American revolutionary application and political philosophy are central. https://nationalhumanitiescenter.org/fellows-books/republics-ancient-and-modern-classical-republicanism-and-the-american-revolution/

Engines of Creation|1986|0|0||6,9,8,8,7,8,10,9,8,8|K. Eric Drexler|Develops a speculative account of molecular manufacturing and its institutional consequences. Physical constraints and engineering possibilities offer transferable thought experiments; feasibility, pathways and timing require much greater uncertainty than a demonstrated technology would. Assessed as qualified technological speculation, not as proof that its projected system exists.

The Closing of the American Mind|1987|10|10||6,7,6,6,6,8,4,9,8,8|Allan Bloom|Critiques university culture through philosophical and literary interpretation. Questions about education and intellectual standards transfer, but selective cultural observations and a sweeping diagnosis reduce evidence and density confidence. Political-cultural advocacy alone does not establish a serious ideological or mobilization veto.

American Nerd: The Story of My People|2008|10|0||7,5,4,4,6,7,3,7,8,7|Benjamin Nugent|Cultural history and reportage examine the formation of a social identity. Distinctions about status and belonging survive removal of personalities, but the argument is remote from technical or strategic mechanisms. American cultural focus incurs T11; not a technical-computing history.

README|2025|0|0||9,9,8,8,8,9,10,9,8,8|W. Patrick McCray|Explains how books helped people understand, adopt and imagine computers. The inspected publisher description and author excerpt connect literary production to technological diffusion and recurrent concerns about machine authorship. Distinct historical examples add constraints; chapter-wide density remains low-confidence. https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262553483/readme/ https://thereader.mitpress.mit.edu/what-is-authorship-when-machines-can-write/
